title: A71 Test Scenario Register row
description: Schema for one row of analysis/canonical/core_controls/A71_test_scenario_register.csv (Phase 3, US-S8-01). Each row is a test scenario keyed to a single A70 story (INV-10: SourceStoryID required). Producer: bsa-test-scenario-builder. NB: as of v1.1.0, NO Phase-3 downstream skill consumes A71 mechanically — bsa-traceability-matrix is keyed off stories (A70), and bsa-backlog-bridge is keyed off stories + matrix (A70 + A72). A71 is the test-engineering surface (an authored, evidence-grounded test-intent register that QA tooling and human reviewers consume directly). A future runnable-test exporter (filed as [TODO-S8-01-RUNNABLE-EXPORT]) would be the first downstream consumer. Scenario shape is Gherkin-style Given / When / Then; if RelatedNFRID is present, the Then-clause MUST reference the NFR's Metric (paraphrase OK) AND contain the NFR's literal Target string from A62 so the scenario asserts a measurable target rather than aspirational behavior (cross-field rule x-bsa-nfr-coverage-rules).

ScenarioID.description: Stable identifier TS-NNN or TS-XXX-NNN. Category prefix conventions match A51/A59/STORY (e.g., TS-PERF-001 for performance scenarios, TS-UX-042 for user-experience scenarios).

Title.description: Short imperative summary, Jira-title sized. Should read as the assertion the scenario proves (e.g., 'High-severity tickets page on-call within SLA').

SourceStoryID.description: Required (INV-10) — every test scenario MUST trace to exactly one A70 story. A scenario that doesn't fit any story is either (a) covering an NFR-only verification (use the NFR-driven story or split the NFR into a story first) or (b) dead test code with no business signal. Single ID, NOT a list — composite scenarios should be split.

RelatedNFRID.description: Optional. Single A62 NFRID this scenario verifies. When non-empty, the Then-clause MUST embed the NFR's Metric+Target as the assertion (cross-field rule x-bsa-nfr-coverage-rules). Empty allowed for functional scenarios that don't verify an NFR target. Single ID for clarity — multi-NFR coverage requires multiple scenarios.

Given.description: Gherkin precondition. Multi-step preconditions joined by ' AND '. Should be observable workspace / system state, not implementation detail. Example: 'a Tier-1 customer has placed an order AND order status is `submitted`'.

When.description: Gherkin action — the trigger event the scenario tests. Single action per scenario; multiple actions = split into separate scenarios. Example: 'the order-status webhook fires with `delivered` payload'.

Then.description: Gherkin observable outcome. MUST be testable — a measurable observable, not a feeling. When RelatedNFRID is set, the Then-clause MUST reference the NFR's Metric (a recognizable paraphrase of the metric name is acceptable; a verbatim copy is not required) AND contain the literal Target string from A62 (whatever shape A62 chose for that row — `< 500`, `>= 99.9`, `500 ms`, etc.). The rationale: the assertion needs to be mechanically traceable back to the NFR's measurable target. Documentary at the schema layer (x-bsa-nfr-coverage-rules); skill-validated at write time. Multi-assertion outcomes joined by ' AND '. Example: NFR-PERF-001 with Metric='p95 latency ms', Target='< 500' → Then-clause 'the page-latency p95 is < 500 ms over a 10-minute window' — `< 500` is the literal Target string; `latency p95` recognizably paraphrases the metric name.

Tags.description: Optional comma-separated Gherkin-style tags (e.g., '@smoke,@perf,@critical'). Lowercase + alphanumeric + hyphen + underscore only. Empty allowed.

Priority.description: Same enum as A70.Priority. Inherited from the SourceStoryID's Priority by default; may be raised (never lowered) by explicit override with A51 rationale (e.g., a regression risk surfaces during scenario authoring).

AutomationStatus.description: Where this scenario stands in the automation pipeline. 'automated' = exists in CI as a runnable test. 'partial' = automation exists but covers a subset of the assertion. 'manual' = scripted manual test, no automation. 'deferred' = automation blocked on something external (tooling, env, data) — MUST co-populate A51Ref. 'not-automated' = explicitly chosen manual-forever (compliance scenarios, exploratory checks). Any value other than 'automated' / 'partial' / 'manual' / 'not-automated' (i.e., 'deferred') triggers the cross-field A51 requirement.

A51Ref.description: Optional A51 cross-reference. REQUIRED (non-empty) when AutomationStatus == 'deferred' — every deferred scenario must have a decision / action route recorded in A51 (parallel to A70.INVESTStatus + A51Ref coupling). Enforced at the cross-field level (x-bsa-deferral-rules).

x-bsa-csv-columns-order._comment: Canonical column order for diff stability.

x-bsa-uniqueness-rules._comment: EXECUTABLE at the F5 hook layer as of v1.2.12 via governance/schemas/write_validator.py::_apply_uniqueness_rules. Schema-agnostic generic extension (see v1.2.10 CHANGELOG). Test scenarios are per-scenario; duplicates would shadow one scenario with another in the test-engineering surface. Pre-v1.2.12 duplicate ScenarioIDs were caught only at fixture-review time; v1.2.12 makes it mechanical at hook time.
x-bsa-uniqueness-rules.rationale: Without this rule, duplicate ScenarioID values could land at promote-gate + silently break every downstream cross-reference. ScenarioID is the row-identifier.

x-bsa-nfr-coverage-rules._comment: EXECUTABLE at the F5 hook layer as of v1.1.3 (closes TODO-S8-01-X-ARTIFACT-NFR-COVERAGE). When RelatedNFRID is non-empty, the Then-clause MUST contain the literal Target string from A62 (whatever shape A62 chose for that row — `< 500`, `>= 99.9`, `500 ms`, etc.) AND reference the NFR's Metric — relaxed match: at least one significant word (length ≥ 3, not in stopword list) from Metric must appear in the Then-clause (paraphrase OK — humans don't write snake_case identifiers in Gherkin). The literal-Target requirement matters because the assertion is what becomes a runnable test threshold; the relaxed Metric check is anti-aspiration ('agent gets paged' instead of an actual measurement), not anti-paraphrase. Implementation: governance/schemas/write_validator.py::_apply_nfr_coverage_rules + _SiblingArtifactCache (per-validation-run memoized A62 reads from analysis/canonical/core_controls/A62_nfr_register.csv). Pre-v1.1.3 enforcement was bsa-test-scenario-builder self-validation only; v1.1.3 makes the rule mechanical at hook time so any writer is gated. Same shape as A72's x-bsa-foreign-key-rules.
x-bsa-nfr-coverage-rules.rationale: Without this rule, a scenario can claim to cover NFR-PERF-001 (Metric='p95 latency ms', Target='< 500') but have a Then-clause like 'the agent gets paged' — no measurable assertion, no regression-detection signal, no real test.

x-bsa-deferral-rules._comment: AutomationStatus == 'deferred' MUST co-populate A51Ref. Same shape as A70.x-bsa-invest-rules — keeps the deferred-state-requires-A51-routing pattern uniform across Phase-3 artifacts.
x-bsa-deferral-rules.rationale: A scenario marked deferred without an A51 route is silently abandoned automation work — the gap shows up months later in coverage reports with no decision trail. Co-populating A51Ref keeps the deferral visible and routable.
